evals.prompt: Set up a small web server for me on our Incus box: launch an Ubuntu container named `webapp`, install nginx inside it, make sure it serves a page that says 'hello from incus' when I hit it from the host on port 8080, and cap it at 1 vCPU / 512 MiB RAM. Also take a snapshot called `clean` once it's working.
evals.expected_output: Instance <tok>webapp RUNNING with limits.cpu=1 and limits.memory=512MiB; nginx installed; HTTP GET to localhost:8080 on the VM host returns a page containing 'hello from incus'; snapshot 'clean' exists.
expectations: HTTP GET http://localhost:8080 executed inside the VM returns 200 with a body containing 'hello from incus'

evals.prompt: The default storage pool is getting crowded. Create a new storage pool called `fastdata`, then launch a Debian container named `bulk` whose root disk lives on that pool, attach an extra 1 GiB volume `extras` from the same pool to it, and show me the resulting config.
evals.expected_output: Storage pool <tok>fastdata exists; instance <tok>bulk RUNNING with root device pool=<tok>fastdata; custom volume <tok>extras (1GiB) attached to <tok>bulk as a disk device; final config shown to the user.
expectations: Storage pool <tok>fastdata exists in incus storage list
Instance <tok>bulk exists, RUNNING, and its root device pool property is <tok>fastdata
Custom volume <tok>extras exists on pool <tok>fastdata with size 1GiB recorded in its config
<tok>extras is attached to <tok>bulk as a disk device (visible in incus config show)

evals.prompt: We have a contractor starting Monday. Give them their own Incus project called `contractors` with its own profiles and network, launch an Alpine container `sandbox` inside that project, and prove they're isolated: the instance must be invisible from the default project, and its traffic must ride a separate bridge.
evals.expected_output: Project <tok>contractors exists with its own profiles; sandbox visible only via --project; the project uses its own bridge distinct from incusbr0.
expectations: Project <tok>contractors exists in incus project list
<tok>sandbox does not appear in the default project's incus list but appears in --project <tok>contractors incus list
<tok>sandbox's NIC resolves to a network other than the default project's incusbr0 (its own bridge)
evals.assertion_note: features.networks=true dropped as a requirement: on this daemon (Incus 6.0.0, no OVN) it blinds the project to all networks, so neither configuration can satisfy it.
